title: Coding a Finite Nondeterministic Machine
statement: For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet, there are a two-work-tape binary-choice machine $M$ with states indexed by an initial segment of the natural numbers and a natural number $C$ such that, for every binary input $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, if $N$ accepts $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $M$ accepts $x$ in exactly $C(t+1)$ steps; conversely, if $M$ accepts $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $N$ accepts $x$ in some number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Bool
